items.summary: This record provides the public reproducibility materials associated with the study The Unequal Cultural City: Functional Differentiation and Spatial Inequality in London’s Cultural Infrastructure . The repository contains analytical code, public-safe derived neighbourhood data, spatial weights, source provenance, methodological protocols, confirmatory and robustness outputs, joint spatial re-estimation results, and supplementary materials for 4,994 Greater London 2021 LSOAs and a 2022 common-vintage cultural-infrastructure dataset. The study measures proximity-weighted availability of recorded cultural infrastructure and distinguishes Production from Encounter/Presentation functions. The two functions strongly overlap spatially. Their most consistently detected direct difference concerns metropolitan centrality: both decline with distance from London’s Central Activities Zone, with a steeper Encounter gradient. The differential deprivation association is model- and construct-sensitive, while the density difference remains unresolved. Cultural sustainability is treated as a bounded implication of the observed infrastructure configuration rather than as a directly measured sustainability outcome. The repository excludes raw site-level address/UPRN data and copyrighted source documents. Exact source provenance, reconstruction instructions, checksums, component-specific rights information, and reproducibility metadata are included.
items.title: Data, Code and Reproducibility Materials for "The Unequal Cultural City: Functional Differentiation and Spatial Inequality in London's Cultural Infrastructure"

items.summary: Analysis code accompanying the main paper and online supplement of “ Reference Observability and Journal Universe Choice in Open Reconstructions of Recursive Journal Metrics ”. The package starts from precomputed Network Factor (NF) and Article Network Score (ANS) inputs released by Opindx.org . It provides downstream statistical analysis, table and figure code, an independently generated fictional demonstration, full open Leiden/CWTS-universe scores, additional open Norwegian-universe nodes, and input and provenance documentation. No proprietary Clarivate data, commercial journal roster or crosswalk, empirical benchmark outputs, or manuscript files are included. Empirical reproduction requires legitimately held benchmark inputs and the author-specific inputs described in docs/INPUTS.md . Fictional demonstration outputs do not reproduce the paper results.
items.title: Replication package for "Reference Observability and Journal Universe Choice in Open Reconstructions of Recursive Journal Metrics"

items.summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) offers millisecond temporal resolution, but inferring underlying neural sources is a severely ill-posed spatial inverse problem. While deep learning has advanced spatial reconstruction, current architectures face a critical dilemma: frame-by-frame models discard vital temporal context, whereas full 4D spatiotemporal networks introduce an architectural trade-off between reconstruction accuracy and inference cost. We propose a novel two-stream framework that explicitly decouples global temporal representation learning from per-time-point spatial refinement. A Transformer-based Temporal Condition Encoder processes the entire EEG sequence via factorized spatiotemporal attention, retaining sensor-resolved features. A fixed inverse then maps these features into source-indexed conditioning for a per-timestep Source-Space Transformer or volumetric convolutional refiner. Extensive evaluations on realistic synthetic data demonstrate that this temporal prior dramatically improves spatial localization, outperforming classical and spatiotemporal baselines, particularly in high-noise and multi-source regimes. Training across diverse leadfields and explicit operator mismatches improves transfer to unseen head geometries and brings template-based reconstruction closer to subject-specific inversion. Furthermore, we apply the model trained only on synthetic EEG data to real-world EEG. A logistic regressor fit on source power differences in eyes-open, eyes-closed conditions successfully decodes age groups.
items.title: Decoupling Time and Space: A Temporally Conditioned Refinement for EEG Source Imaging

items.summary: Recovering the forward operator of an imaging system from unpaired data avoids both calibration hardware and the clean/degraded pairs that supervision requires-pairs that, for a real lens, are often impossible to acquire. Existing unpaired approaches that explicitly estimate the forward operator by distribution matching evaluate a candidate only through the measurements it generates, whose distribution should match that of the real ones. Components suppressed by the operator are barely present in the degraded images, and therefore barely constrain the operator under such a criterion. Yet inversion precisely tries to recover them. As a result, two operators that are nearly indistinguishable as forward models can invert very differently. We address this by adding a comparison on the clean side: real degraded images, once restored, should be distributed like clean ones. Restorations are computed by a differentiable plug-and-play algorithm parameterized by the operator being learned. On spatially varying PSF calibration and blind super-resolution, the method recovers more accurate operators than degraded-side matching alone, and closes much of the gap to restoration with the true operator.
items.title: Reconstruction-Aware Distribution Matching for Inverse Problems with Unpaired Data

items.summary: First versioned journal-submission release for: Learning When Black Hole Hair Is Observable: Physical Identifiability, Generalization, and Observable Complementarity This release contains the publication-facing Kiselev black hole identifiability benchmark, including: validated timelike-emitter and 3D direct null-geodesic shooting; Jacobian identifiability diagnostics; leakage-aware random, grouped, and directional inverse-learning protocols; non-learned nearest-model and local-Jacobian baselines; 81-, 161-, and targeted 321-phase numerical-resolution audits; observation-facing redshift and signed-sky sensitivity analysis; manuscript source and compiled manuscript PDF; publication figures, machine-readable derived results, and reproducibility tests. This is a theoretical identifiability benchmark and does not constitute an observational constraint on black hole hair.
items.title: Learning When Black Hole Hair Is Observable: Physical Identifiability, Generalization, and Observable Complementarity

items.summary: World action models (WAMs) predict actions and future observations, typically from a reconstruction-based representation that carries noisy, redundant information which can complicate downstream predictions. We introduce LeWAM, a bidirectional transformer for forward, backward, inverse dynamics and policy prediction, on a decoder-free JEPA latent trained end-to-end through all four modes. We see the following benefits: 1) Alignment: linear probes read robot and object state from LeWAM's latent better than from a regular Le World Model (a forward-only JEPA world model), while the latent ignores visual distractors as well as LeWM does and far better than a reconstruction-based WAM. 2) Acting: Closed-loop evaluations of LeWAM match a regular flow-matching policy trained on the same encoder at matched size, while also providing a world model. 3) Planning: Sampling raw actions when planning with WAMs lets MPC exploit dynamics-model inaccuracies; planning in the noise space of the policy head instead improves the closed-loop performance of these WAMs.
items.title: LeWAM: A JEPA World Action Model with Diffusion-Steering-Based MPC

items.summary: What if an AI agent could not complete a consequential action until the real-world result of an earlier, bounded action had been independently verified—and that verification was required to unlock the next execution step? As frontier AI models and autonomous agents increasingly operate financial systems, cloud infrastructure, sensitive communications, autonomous machinery, and critical infrastructure, conventional security mechanisms face a fundamental limitation: authorization establishes what is permitted, but does not necessarily establish what actually happened along the real execution path. Audit logs may record a mistake after its consequences become irreversible. Simulations may succeed while the real destination, network route, transaction system, or physical actuator behaves differently. Even a successful initial authorization does not justify unlimited authority to execute subsequent actions. This paper develops a different architectural principle: “Evidence is the key, not the log.” Building on the distinction that computation is not authority to act , the proposed architecture makes independently validated evidence of a preceding real effect a technical prerequisite for later effectuation. The mechanism is called Receipt-Gated Staged Effectuation , supported by an Interim Effectuation Validator (IEV) . For selected consequential operations, the architecture authorizes a deliberately bounded but real first effect, rather than immediately releasing the complete consequence. A protected observer, destination, transaction system, network element, storage component, or hardware controller generates an Effect Confirmation Receipt (ECR) describing what actually occurred. The IEV independently verifies the receipt against the authorized Candidate Act, expected effect, phase, destination, sink identity, freshness, policy, revocation state, and authorized scope. Only after successful validation does the protected domain establish the Continuation Authority Object (CAO) required for the next phase. The critical distinction is that the next effect can be made technically impossible—not merely prohibited by policy—until validated evidence from the preceding real effect becomes available. Possible implementations include receipt-derived cryptographic keys, split-key reconstruction, protected internal state, hardware latches, pre-staged non-executable commands, and pre-delivered ciphertext whose final decryption material remains withheld. Unlike ordinary canary deployment or post-execution monitoring, the earlier phase's evidence becomes part of the causal authority chain. Its receipt is not merely information about the previous operation; it is a required input to the authority enabling the next operation. The paper develops: Three effectuation modes: Direct protected single-phase execution, bounded demonstration followed by full effectuation, and progressive multi-phase execution. Adaptive effectuation: Geometric and risk-dependent progression, reversibility-aware phase sizing, nested stages, and parallel effectuation. Cryptographic causal dependency: Receipt-derived execution material, split credentials, tokenless continuation, hardware-gated enablement, and protected state transitions. Protected evidence semantics: Proof of delivery versus proof of effect, negative receipts, receipt freshness, destination binding, cross-device protection, Merkle receipt structures, and privacy-preserving confirmation. Independent continuation authority: Human, automatic, hybrid, and multi-authority decisions separated from the potentially compromised AI-agent environment. Fail-closed recovery: Missing or conflicting receipts, uncertain outcomes, replay protection, atomic consumption, reconciliation, and prevention of blind retries. Anti-bypass enforcement: Protected execution boundaries, credential surrogation, taint and provenance controls, alternative-path closure, and software–hardware implementation ind
items.title: Evidence Is the Key, Not the Log: Cryptographic Execution Control for AI Agents and Autonomous Systems

items.summary: This record provides the reproducibility archive accompanying the manuscript “Frontier Mutual Information: Structured Global Inference from Local Contrasts” by Tsutomu Mori and Takashi Kawamura. The manuscript develops frontier mutual information as a framework for structured local-to-global inference, investigating when informative local contrasts can be used to recover or constrain global mutual information. This archive contains the computational materials supporting the study, including source code, synthetic data, reference outputs, publication-figure generation materials, paper-to-artifact mappings, documentation, and integrity and verification files. It also includes materials for independent verification of the numerical and finite-sample results reported in the manuscript. The archive is intended to enable transparent inspection, independent reproduction, and verification of the computational results. The theoretical claims, assumptions, and scope of applicability should be interpreted according to the accompanying manuscript.
items.title: Frontier Mutual Information: Structured Global Inference from Local Contrasts — Reproducibility Archive

items.summary: Version 1.2.0 is the corrected scope-limited public release accompanying Single-realization evaluation can misclassify task-specific synthetic-data suitability across clinical destinations. The archive contains the exact tested public code commit b2171fca115412b22dff0961420a594ef2423fe6, approved aggregate source projections and two supplementary workbooks, and fully fabricated demonstration outputs. Software authority: https://github.com/woshizh321/synthetic-icu-fit-for-purpose-evaluation/releases/tag/v1.2.0-public-scope. Local fresh clone/install and two independent Ubuntu runner jobs each passed all 61 public tests at the unchanged 1e-6 tolerance. The numerical correction uses centered three-point gradient evaluation on the same objective and estimand; frozen expected values and scientific results are unchanged. No patient-level clinical records, individual predictions, evaluated synthetic rows, clinical model weights, generator checkpoints, source hospital identifiers, hospital-indexed restricted derivatives, private mappings, or historical split/bootstrap assets are distributed. Public aggregate reproduction and fabricated-fixture execution are supported within the documented scope; this archive does not establish complete historical clinical reconstruction. Exact historical MIMIC split replay requires restricted assets. eICU canonical-to-analysis equivalence is verified, while raw CSV-to-canonical reconstruction is not independently verified and historical D-09 execution source remains unresolved. No clinical scientific analysis was rerun. This corrected version supersedes earlier release-scope claims. Aggregate results and documentation retain CC BY 4.0; original code is MIT; upstream software and source clinical databases retain their own terms.
items.title: Reproducibility materials for stochastic evaluation of synthetic ICU data across generator realizations and clinical destinations

items.summary: This repository contains the computational code, numerical inputs, output tables, and audit records supporting the study “Electrothermal Modelling, Detectability, and Robustness of a Rhombohedral GeTe Thin-Film Dual-Mode Sensor: A Literature-Constrained Multiphysics Study". The package provides the reproducible workflow used for the revised electrothermal calculations, including electrical power-budget analysis, three-dimensional thermal reconstruction, transient-response calculations, thermal-boundary sensitivity, contact-resistivity sensitivity, uncertainty propagation, and supporting verification records. The repository is intended to enable independent reproduction and inspection of the computational results reported in the manuscript. The study is literature-constrained and computational; the deposited files should not be interpreted as experimental calibration of a fabricated GeTe device
items.title: Reproducibility Package for "Electrothermal Modelling, Detectability, and Robustness of a Rhombohedral GeTe Thin-Film Dual-Mode Sensor: A Literature-Constrained Multiphysics Study"

items.summary: This dataset supports the study “A methodological evaluation of deposited-assembly usability and raw-read rescue in a global public Klebsiella pneumoniae genome collection.” It contains accession-level manifests, derived statistical tables, figure-source data, documentation, software-version information, and analysis code. Of 44,278 geographically resolved eligible records, 1,670 were used in another study and excluded from this analysis. Seventeen were excluded because their deposited assemblies did not meet the input criteria and raw-read download attempts were unsuccessful. The historical analyzable-input manifest therefore contained 42,591 records (40,094 public assemblies and 2,497 raw-derived inputs). Species adjudication excluded one record from each source, leaving 42,589 genomes: 40,093 public assemblies and 2,496 raw-derived genomes. Thirteen failed or unfinished raw-read attempts were retained through the public-assembly pathway and are not included in the 1,687 exclusions. Version 1.5.0 adds BioProject mapping for all 42,589 final genomes across 340 projects, descriptive project-level sensitivity analyses, updated record-disposition tables, and revised Figure 1 and Figure S1 materials. The locked primary cohort and primary statistical results remain unchanged. Exact-category sensitivity endpoints differ from the grouped primary endpoints; equal-project-weighted analyses and project bootstrap intervals are exploratory. Genome assemblies and raw reads were retrieved using a combination of scripts, download utilities, and manual downloads from repository webpages. Deposited assemblies were assessed first, with raw-read reconstruction attempted when a deposited assembly could not be retrieved or did not meet the input criteria. Exact historical read preprocessing commands could not be recovered. Adapter-trimming and quality-filtering parameters are outside this deposit’s reproducibility claim. Record-level logs documenting the 17 exclusions were unavailable. The deposit does not redistribute genome assemblies or raw sequencing reads. Retrieve sequence data from the original repositories using the supplied accession identifiers. Archived code supports the post-assembly cohort checks, primary statistical summaries, and BioProject sensitivity analyses. Jianhua Li and Jing Guo contributed equally. Jing Chen is the corresponding author (dongqingfei@126.com). Funding: Natural Science Foundation of Xiamen Municipality (3502Z202373092) and Xiamen Medical and Health Guidance Project (3502Z20254ZD1079).
items.title: Data and analysis materials for: A methodological evaluation of deposited-assembly usability and raw-read rescue in a global public Klebsiella pneumoniae genome collection

items.summary: This record provides the public, non-confidential analytical and reproducibility materials supporting the manuscript “When Does Seismic–Geotechnical Data Fusion Add Value? A Borehole-Aware Empirical-to-Synthetic Validation Framework for Urban Tunnelling.” The study develops and audits a borehole-aware empirical-to-synthetic framework for evaluating whether adding downhole seismic information provides defensible incremental value in predicting the Ménard pressuremeter modulus under held-out validation. The empirical benchmark comprises 41 support-matched pressuremeter–seismic records across 21 independent boreholes from the Isfahan Metro Line 2 investigation. The framework compares a reference model, a geotechnical/geological-depth baseline, a seismic-only branch, naive multimodal fusion, and a dependence-aware fusion branch using leave-one-borehole-out validation. The public release contains a de-identified 41-record benchmark dataset, final manuscript Figure 1–5 assets, the current Supplementary Material and Supplementary Figure S1, released derived analytical outputs, provenance and reproducibility documentation, reproducibility and repository-audit scripts, computational-environment specifications, and SHA-256 integrity information. The de-identified dataset replaces source borehole identifiers with pseudonymous identifiers and excludes borehole coordinates and other spatially identifying source information. The underlying Isfahan Metro Line 2 geotechnical, geophysical, and pressuremeter source records are controlled by the Isfahan Urban Railway Organization and are not publicly redistributable. Original source workbooks, proprietary project documents, spatially identifying information, and other restricted source-derived materials are intentionally excluded from this public archive. Permission was obtained to use and publish the de-identified, non-confidential data extracted from the project report and the derived analytical information included in this release. The public code component provides scripts for reproducing the released manuscript-level benchmark metrics and verifying the integrity and consistency of the deposited files. These scripts do not contain the restricted original project records or proprietary source-data processing materials. The archive is intended to support transparent audit and reproducibility of the released derived analyses while preserving the access restrictions applying to the underlying project data.
items.title: When Does Seismic–Geotechnical Data Fusion Add Value? — Project 06 Data and Reproducibility Package

items.summary: Self-contained computational materials accompanying "Verifiable approval-release decisions for construction project management: A provenance-aware contract and automated evidence" by Ahmad Baghdadi. Version 4.0.0 includes source code, complete generated inputs and results, schemas, exact witnesses, a de-identified calendar encoding, benchmark records and SHA-256 checksums. This version adds 83 conventional priority-list levelling comparisons under identical constraints: 72 tied peaks and 11 one-gate improvements, with sufficient exact certificates for all 83. A complete two-plan PROV-O example passes the domain and provenance SHACL profiles and preserves every decision field after RDF exchange. The suite comprises 145 automated tests. Earlier computational evidence includes generated extraction, 360 controlled record comparisons, exact wave bounds, nine calendar scenarios and 80 saved benchmark plans with renewed arithmetic audit. S14 preparation includes blank independent-annotation and approval registers plus a precision/recall evaluator with explicit denominators. No native baseline or independent annotations are available; field validation has not been executed. Case A remains historical aggregates only. Calendar B is a prior encoding with assumed review windows. Supplementary Table S1 identifies the deposited components and the supplement consolidates the evidence limits.
items.title: Reproducibility materials for verifiable approval-release decisions in construction project management

items.summary: Code, preregistration record and derived data for a manuscript submitted to Environmental Impact Assessment Review. audit.py reproduces every figure and number in the paper through twenty-one pipeline stages and writes a per-stage log with stdout hashes; the last stage checks that every number printed in the manuscript and its tables is traceable to a file the pipeline writes, and exits non-zero if one is not. The deposit contains the analysis scripts, the preregistration record with its revision history, the derived per-point attributes for the 799 labelled points — lithological class and fault distance — the literature weight extraction, the figures, the audit log, and the anonymized manuscript and supplementary material that the last stage reads. The primary sources are not redistributed: the geological mapping and fault traces of the Hellenic Survey of Geology and Mineral Exploration are available under institutional access only. See README.md for each source and its access terms; MANIFEST.txt lists every deposited file with its md5. Changes since v1.1: the target journal is Environmental Impact Assessment Review rather than Omega; a twenty-first stage checks the provenance of every number in the submitted documents; the comparison of the two lithological codings is a stage rather than two runs sequenced by hand, after a clean pass was found to leave both codings’ outputs holding the same distribution; the Fisher’s exact test of the permeability contrast, previously computed outside the pipeline, is computed by the script that draws Figure S2; the figure scripts share figstyle.py, which embeds TrueType fonts and pins the font family, after two runs of the same pipeline produced figures in two different typefaces; fig2.py and fig3.py, which produce two of the submitted figures, were added to the audit, having been outside it; range_weights.py replaces a script that had been deleted; rapidfuzz is declared in requirements.txt after a silent fallback had changed the scheme count from 129 to 125; and make_deposit.py builds the archive from an explicit list instead of by hand.
items.title: Code and derived data for: Can decision records validate criterion weights? Resampling evidence from 73 documented siting decisions

items.summary: Version 1.1.0 makes a typed RASS evidence extension the representation backbone beneath the action-specific evidence contract. Its full-domain quantitative core follows the real amply soft-set (RASS) representation, while categorical payload, evidence status, provenance and acquisition metadata remain separate companions. Native records are projected onto a 29-coordinate universe with nested T0--T3 active sets; scalars, genuine intervals, categorical values and explicit empty-state reasons retain their native semantics. Audits confirm 192/192 enumerated routing-state matches, exact projection of 80/80 frozen held-out feature entries and 80/80 required-coordinate inactivity checks. A content-addressed contract manifest records the representation, support, action, loss, risk denominators and frozen artifact hashes; an outcome-blind refinement audit verifies nested qualification sets at 300, 360 and 500 cycles and binds all 60 frozen horizon-specific decisions to unique traces. The evidence contract supplies authorization semantics, while the frozen predictor, calibration, held-out decisions and empirical results remain unchanged. The package includes the immutable pre-open snapshot, derived development and external-admissibility audits, unit tests, figures and file-level SHA-256 manifests. Raw provider datasets and private overlap ledgers are not redistributed.
items.title: Evidence-contract knowledge system for auditable second-life battery qualification: reproducibility package

items.summary: Analysis code and computed evidence store for the manuscript "An exact recurrence test for acquisition-chain bounds in vehicle telemetry: the closed ECU surface yields nothing, and the one detection lies in the logger we built ourselves", submitted to Sensors and Actuators A: Physical. This deposit contains code and derived results only. The underlying telemetry is published separately under its own DOIs, which fetch_data.py downloads and checksum-verifies before analysis, so the published figures are reproducible from the public record. Study design: observational audit of already-deposited telemetry (seven recording sessions). No experimental control, no intervention, no independent replication, and no statistical power for population-level inference. Headlines formulated after measurement rather than pre-declared in config.json are labelled exploratory in the manuscript. Multiplicity: this deposit is one of 15 analyses drawn from the same corpus of seven sessions, one vehicle and one rider. No correction for multiple comparisons is applied across that family, so the family-wise error rate is not controlled. Repository commit of record: 37f7b2147b26
items.title: Reproducibility package (I-21): An exact recurrence test for acquisition-chain bounds in vehicle telemetry: the closed ECU surface yields nothing, and the one detection lies in the logger we built ourselves

items.summary: Source code for Skillarum: Conditionally Reproducible Website-to-Agent-Skill Compilation. Skillarum turns selected public website pages into portable SKILL.md documents for agent harnesses such as Codex, Claude Code, and Hermes, in five inspectable stages (acquire, prepare, process, parse, render) with provenance manifests and an evidence-gated research package. Release 0.3.0 added index-derived profiles (one skill per page listed on a site's own index; 528 Math 4 Wisdom Research pages), block-preserving extraction, authored target descriptions, and math4wisdom-cube, a versioned investigation skill with separate source, mathematics, interpretation, and test ledgers, audited by three independent AI investigators whose verbatim reports are included. Release 0.3.1 is a correction release: math4wisdom-cube 0.3.0 withdraws an investigator claim that 0.2.0 adopted without recomputation (1+3+3+1 is not the generic grading pattern) and adds a check for the corrected statement; the changelog's account of investigator independence and two documentation statements are corrected.
items.title: Skillarum: Conditionally Reproducible Website-to-Agent-Skill Compilation

items.summary: Supporting research data for physical-state supervision of design-only Gaussian process surrogates, with optional mixture-of-experts comparisons. Includes 1,987 CH designs, 3,000 thermal-explosion designs, 3,000 recalculated Be/Cocktail designs, state diagnostics, saved predictions, paired evaluation metrics, learning curves, grid diagnostics, timing records and file-level provenance. The data record does not include software, solver binaries, material libraries or raw trajectories. Grid sensitivities and historical reproduction limitations are documented in README.md. Data and accompanying documentation are licensed under CC BY 4.0.
items.title: Physical-state supervision for design-only Gaussian process surrogates of implosion simulations: supporting data

items.summary: Long-horizon robotic manipulation is often built by chaining independently trained skills. Although each skill can be reliable in isolation, performance degrades sharply when skills are chained: each downstream skill must start from the state its predecessor leaves behind rather than from its training distribution. We study this failure mode, Observation-Space Shift (OSS), and ask what causes these skill-seam failures. Using privileged simulator resets, we find that the dominant shift comes from displaced scene state (e.g., an open drawer or secondary objects left behind by earlier skills), not from the robot's joint configuration or the object the downstream skill manipulates. To test this diagnosis, we build a fully learned detect-restore-resume system: a task-progress monitor detects the stall, a learned policy restores the displaced scene components, and seam-robust fine-tuning lets the skill resume. It recovers the seam where every tested alternative fails, which we treat as evidence for the diagnosis rather than as a general-purpose method. On the BOSS-44 benchmark, the system improves full-chain success from 7.6% to 26.5%, a 3.5x improvement over the base policy and 51% of a privileged restoration oracle, whereas best-of-K resampling, a Diffusion Policy, and world-model baselines fail to recover from the evaluated seam states. On a real Franka arm running a fine-tuned $π_{0.5}$ policy, the same monitor is limited by exterior-camera observability, yet closing the loop still recovers some otherwise-terminal failures, motivating wrist and gripper sensing. These results suggest that some long-horizon composition failures are better addressed by restoring the scene before resuming the policy than by retrying from an off-support state.
items.title: Diagnosing and Recovering from Observation-Space Shift at Long-Horizon Skill Seams

items.summary: Data video is a media form that integrates data visualization with video narrative, widely adopted in news reporting and business analysis. Compared with general video understanding, data video understanding places greater emphasis on accurately reading data from animated charts, integrating evidence across charts and time, and understanding how narrative organization and visual design communicate information. Yet existing benchmarks target either general videos or static charts, and data video understanding has not been systematically evaluated. We present DataVista, the first benchmark for data video understanding, containing 961 real-world data videos and 6,775 evaluation questions organized under a three-level progressive capability framework (data perception, temporal reasoning, narrative understanding) with 10 fine-grained question types across five topic domains. Systematic evaluation of 19 mainstream MLLMs shows that the best-performing model, Gemini-3.1-Pro, achieves 70.0% overall accuracy, still far below human expert performance, with models performing worst on Causal Reasoning and Narrative Structure. Increasing frame counts and adding subtitles mainly benefit data perception and temporal reasoning, with limited gains in narrative understanding. Further analysis of model responses identifies typical failure modes in chart reading, evidence judgment, and instruction understanding. The benchmark is available at https://github.com/HKUSTDial/DataVista.
items.title: DataVista: Diagnosing Multimodal LLMs on Data Video Understanding

The benchmark is available at https://github.com/HKUSTDial/DataVista.
items.title: DataVista: Diagnosing Multimodal LLMs on Data Video Understanding

items.summary: This dataset supports the study “A methodological evaluation of deposited-assembly usability and raw-read rescue in a global public Klebsiella pneumoniae genome collection.” It contains accession-level manifests, derived statistical tables, figure-source data, documentation, software-version information, and analysis code. Of 44,278 geographically resolved eligible records, 1,670 were used in another study and excluded from this analysis. Seventeen were excluded because their deposited assemblies did not meet the input criteria and raw-read download attempts were unsuccessful. The historical analyzable-input manifest therefore contained 42,591 records (40,094 public assemblies and 2,497 raw-derived inputs). Species adjudication excluded one record from each source, leaving 42,589 genomes: 40,093 public assemblies and 2,496 raw-derived genomes. Thirteen failed or unfinished raw-read attempts were retained through the public-assembly pathway and are not included in the 1,687 exclusions. Version 1.5.0 adds BioProject mapping for all 42,589 final genomes across 340 projects, descriptive project-level sensitivity analyses, updated record-disposition tables, and revised Figure 1 and Figure S1 materials. The locked primary cohort and primary statistical results remain unchanged. Exact-category sensitivity endpoints differ from the grouped primary endpoints; equal-project-weighted analyses and project bootstrap intervals are exploratory. Genome assemblies and raw reads were retrieved using a combination of scripts, download utilities, and manual downloads from repository webpages. Deposited assemblies were assessed first, with raw-read reconstruction attempted when a deposited assembly could not be retrieved or did not meet the input criteria. Exact historical read preprocessing commands could not be recovered. Adapter-trimming and quality-filtering parameters are outside this deposit’s reproducibility claim. Record-level logs documenting the 17 exclusions were unavailable. The deposit does not redistribute genome assemblies or raw sequencing reads. Retrieve sequence data from the original repositories using the supplied accession identifiers. Archived code supports the post-assembly cohort checks, primary statistical summaries, and BioProject sensitivity analyses. Jianhua Li and Jing Guo contributed equally. Jing Chen is the corresponding author (dongqingfei@126.com). Funding: Natural Science Foundation of Xiamen Municipality (3502Z202373092) and Xiamen Medical and Health Guidance Project (3502Z20254ZD1079).
items.title: Data and analysis materials for: A methodological evaluation of deposited-assembly usability and raw-read rescue in a global public Klebsiella pneumoniae genome collection

items.summary: Self-contained computational materials accompanying "Verifiable approval-release decisions for construction project management: A provenance-aware contract and automated evidence" by Ahmad Baghdadi. Version 4.0.0 includes source code, complete generated inputs and results, schemas, exact witnesses, a de-identified calendar encoding, benchmark records and SHA-256 checksums. This version adds 83 conventional priority-list levelling comparisons under identical constraints: 72 tied peaks and 11 one-gate improvements, with sufficient exact certificates for all 83. A complete two-plan PROV-O example passes the domain and provenance SHACL profiles and preserves every decision field after RDF exchange. The suite comprises 145 automated tests. Earlier computational evidence includes generated extraction, 360 controlled record comparisons, exact wave bounds, nine calendar scenarios and 80 saved benchmark plans with renewed arithmetic audit. S14 preparation includes blank independent-annotation and approval registers plus a precision/recall evaluator with explicit denominators. No native baseline or independent annotations are available; field validation has not been executed. Case A remains historical aggregates only. Calendar B is a prior encoding with assumed review windows. Supplementary Table S1 identifies the deposited components and the supplement consolidates the evidence limits.

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a comment on a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview and comments at https://prereview.org/reviews/22745390 . Thank you, Evgenii, for the detailed and constructive PREreview. Your comments led us to substantially strengthen both the experimental design and the interpretation of the results. We have now released a revised version of the manuscript that addresses the main points raised in the review. The revision includes: A 30-seed robustness analysis rather than relying on a single simulation seed A correlation sweep for estimator errors from ρ = 0 to 0.8 Regression-fitted and test-set oracle aggregation baselines Shared-noise experiments for the model–collective calibration signal, reported with ROC-AUC and lift Explicit specification of the four-Wave rolling calibration window, software versions, and PCG64 RNG Portfolio scaling to 100 Feature Blocks using an exact binary MILP reference An explicit separation between budget-constrained portfolio selection and ODP's native dependency-aware sequencing role An exact and scaling benchmark for ODP sequencing under prerequisite constraints An explicit competing-interest disclosure A public reproducibility package containing the simulation code, deterministic seeds, generated data, analysis scripts, and validation material. One particularly useful outcome of the revision was that the stronger experiments narrowed some of our original claims. For example, inverse-MSE aggregation performs very strongly when estimator errors are independent, but its advantage collapses under strong shared error. We also found that ODP distance is not the strongest heuristic for budget-constrained portfolio selection, while it performs very differently in its native sequencing role, where ERS/BVS is exactly optimal for the declared objective without dependencies and remains close to the exact optimum under the tested prerequisite constraints. Revised manuscript: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10648 Reproducibility package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23261325 Thank you again for the review. It improved the paper. Competing interests I am a co-author of the manuscript discussed in this PREreview and a contributor to the D-POAF framework evaluated in the study. I am also affiliated with Inovionix, which develops software implementing D-POAF concepts.
items.title: Comment on a PREreview of "Governed Human-AI Prioritization Under Uncertainty: Adaptive Estimation and Dependency-Constrained Portfolio Selection"

items.summary: The present study was undertaken to establish pharmacognostic standards and phytochemical profiles of two ethnomedicinally important plants, Cajanus goensis and Sarcostigma kleinii. Both species are traditionally employed in the treatment of rheumatism, inflammatory disorders, and other systemic ailments, yet scientific validation of their crude drug parameters remains limited. Standardization of herbal materials is essential to ensure identity, purity, and reproducibility, thereby reducing variability and enhancing therapeutic reliability. In this study, plant materials were procured from authentic local sources—Cajanus goensis from Udaipur, Rajasthan, and Sarcostigma kleinii from Latur, Maharashtra—and subjected to comprehensive pharmacognostic and phytochemical evaluation. Organoleptic analysis revealed distinct sensory characteristics, with Cajanus goensis exhibiting greenish-brown coloration, earthy odor, and coarse texture, while Sarcostigma kleinii showed yellowish-brown coloration, pungent odor, and oily texture. Macroscopic and microscopic examinations confirmed diagnostic features such as dorsiventral leaves, reticulate venation, thick cuticular layers, and prominent vascular bundles. Physico-chemical evaluation demonstrated that ash values, extractive values, moisture content, and pH were within pharmacopoeial limits, thereby confirming the purity and stability of the crude drugs. Notably, Cajanus goensis exhibited higher alcohol-soluble extractives, while Sarcostigma kleinii showed greater water-soluble extractives, reflecting differences in phytoconstituent solubility. Phytochemical screening revealed the presence of carbohydrates, amino acids, alkaloids, glycosides, flavonoids, tannins, and phenolic compounds in both species. Proteins were detected only in Sarcostigma kleinii, while saponins were present exclusively in Cajanus goensis. Sterols were absent in both plants, highlighting unique chemical signatures that aid in authentication. Quantitative estimation confirmed that both species are rich in flavonoids and phenolic compounds, with Sarcostigma kleinii showing slightly higher concentrations (21.06 ± 1.000 mg/g quercetin equivalents and 21.19 ± 0.854 mg/g tannic acid equivalents) compared to Cajanus goensis (19.09 ± 0.444 mg/g and 18.49 ± 0.033 mg/g, respectively). These bioactive constituents are well recognized for their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, supporting the traditional use of these plants in rheumatism and related disorders. In conclusion, the study provides reproducible pharmacognostic and phytochemical data for Cajanus goensis and Sarcostigma kleinii, thereby validating their ethnomedicinal claims and establishing a foundation for further pharmacological investigations. The results underscore the importance of standardization in herbal medicine and highlight the potential of these crude drugs as reliable sources of bioactive compounds for future therapeutic applications.
tags: Cajanus goensis; Sarcostigma kleinii; crude drug standardization; phytochemical screening; flavonoids; phenolic compounds; rheumatism; pharmacognosy; herbal medicine; quality control.
items.title: Standardization And Phytochemical Profiling of Cajanus Goensis and Sarcostigma Kleinii: Establishing Baseline Parameters for Crude Drug Evaluation

items.summary: Version 1.1.0 makes a typed RASS evidence extension the representation backbone beneath the action-specific evidence contract. Its full-domain quantitative core follows the real amply soft-set (RASS) representation, while categorical payload, evidence status, provenance and acquisition metadata remain separate companions. Native records are projected onto a 29-coordinate universe with nested T0--T3 active sets; scalars, genuine intervals, categorical values and explicit empty-state reasons retain their native semantics. Audits confirm 192/192 enumerated routing-state matches, exact projection of 80/80 frozen held-out feature entries and 80/80 required-coordinate inactivity checks. A content-addressed contract manifest records the representation, support, action, loss, risk denominators and frozen artifact hashes; an outcome-blind refinement audit verifies nested qualification sets at 300, 360 and 500 cycles and binds all 60 frozen horizon-specific decisions to unique traces. The evidence contract supplies authorization semantics, while the frozen predictor, calibration, held-out decisions and empirical results remain unchanged. The package includes the immutable pre-open snapshot, derived development and external-admissibility audits, unit tests, figures and file-level SHA-256 manifests. Raw provider datasets and private overlap ledgers are not redistributed.
items.title: Evidence-contract knowledge system for auditable second-life battery qualification: reproducibility package

items.summary: Replication package for a validation study of three off-the-shelf sentiment instruments (SenticNet 9, VADER, Twitter-RoBERTa) against blind three-coder human annotation on a stratified audit sample of 504 tweets, drawn from a collection of English-language tweets directed at six European airlines in the summers of 2018-2022 (252,650 user tweets after removal of re-captured records). The package contains, with no tweet text: tweet-level labels of all three instruments for every collected record (re-captured records and truncated author identifiers flagged); the 504 audited items with all three coders' original ratings, the original majority consensus, the post-audit adjudications and completed ratings, and a text-free linkage summary of each audited item's capture multiplicity; the codebook; the VADER and Twitter-RoBERTa scorers with the model revision; a conda environment manifest; and a single script (code/reproduce_all.py) that regenerates every statistic in the manuscript's tables, including the multiplicity-adjusted stratified difference estimates. See README.md for the layout, the sampling note, and the reproducibility boundaries (the historical SenticNet API run cannot be re-executed; the corpus cannot be rehydrated because platform identifiers were truncated at collection).
items.title: Replication package: Sentiment Instruments Are Not Interchangeable — Audited Validity, Its Descriptive Consequences, and Its Correction in Airline-Directed Twitter Discourse

items.summary: Code, preregistration record and derived data for a manuscript submitted to Environmental Impact Assessment Review. audit.py reproduces every figure and number in the paper through twenty-one pipeline stages and writes a per-stage log with stdout hashes; the last stage checks that every number printed in the manuscript and its tables is traceable to a file the pipeline writes, and exits non-zero if one is not. The deposit contains the analysis scripts, the preregistration record with its revision history, the derived per-point attributes for the 799 labelled points — lithological class and fault distance — the literature weight extraction, the figures, the audit log, and the anonymized manuscript and supplementary material that the last stage reads. The primary sources are not redistributed: the geological mapping and fault traces of the Hellenic Survey of Geology and Mineral Exploration are available under institutional access only. See README.md for each source and its access terms; MANIFEST.txt lists every deposited file with its md5. Changes since v1.1: the target journal is Environmental Impact Assessment Review rather than Omega; a twenty-first stage checks the provenance of every number in the submitted documents; the comparison of the two lithological codings is a stage rather than two runs sequenced by hand, after a clean pass was found to leave both codings’ outputs holding the same distribution; the Fisher’s exact test of the permeability contrast, previously computed outside the pipeline, is computed by the script that draws Figure S2; the figure scripts share figstyle.py, which embeds TrueType fonts and pins the font family, after two runs of the same pipeline produced figures in two different typefaces; fig2.py and fig3.py, which produce two of the submitted figures, were added to the audit, having been outside it; range_weights.py replaces a script that had been deleted; rapidfuzz is declared in requirements.txt after a silent fallback had changed the scheme count from 129 to 125; and make_deposit.py builds the archive from an explicit list instead of by hand.
items.title: Code and derived data for: Can decision records validate criterion weights? Resampling evidence from 73 documented siting decisions

items.summary: Source code for Skillarum: Conditionally Reproducible Website-to-Agent-Skill Compilation. Skillarum turns selected public website pages into portable SKILL.md documents for agent harnesses such as Codex, Claude Code, and Hermes, in five inspectable stages (acquire, prepare, process, parse, render) with provenance manifests and an evidence-gated research package. Release 0.3.0 added index-derived profiles (one skill per page listed on a site's own index; 528 Math 4 Wisdom Research pages), block-preserving extraction, authored target descriptions, and math4wisdom-cube, a versioned investigation skill with separate source, mathematics, interpretation, and test ledgers, audited by three independent AI investigators whose verbatim reports are included. Release 0.3.1 is a correction release: math4wisdom-cube 0.3.0 withdraws an investigator claim that 0.2.0 adopted without recomputation (1+3+3+1 is not the generic grading pattern) and adds a check for the corrected statement; the changelog's account of investigator independence and two documentation statements are corrected.
items.title: Skillarum: Conditionally Reproducible Website-to-Agent-Skill Compilation

items.summary: A book in progress on agentic coding and agentic research, compiled from the repository that is its evidence, written around one problem: moving the expensive kernels of the WAVEWATCH III (WW3) third-generation spectral wind-wave model to GPUs without changing the answer. Seventeen lessons, built into a PDF on every merge, from the wave spectrum to running the Fortran model on real cases with a pinned Nix toolchain and annotated switch files. Benchmarks on CPU (OpenMP, MPI) and GPU (OpenACC, CUDA Fortran), each number with the command that reproduces it. A C++/Kokkos port of W3SNL1, the Discrete Interaction Approximation (DIA) of nonlinear four-wave interactions, written with coding agents and shown bit-identical to the Fortran on the Serial, OpenMP and CUDA backends by a field-by-field parity harness. The method itself: the rules coding agents follow here, design docs with a definition of done (WFIPs), decision records (ADRs), a research log, and plans whose every claim carries its evidence. Includes runnable examples, exercises with solutions, and an undergraduate project proposal (Escola Politécnica, UFRJ, co-advised at LabECO, UFSC).
items.title: WW3 GPU Lab: agentic coding and agentic research on a bit-for-bit GPU port of WAVEWATCH III

items.summary: daf-jev 0.7.2 provides typed native decision clients, provider-neutral backends, pure composition, exact discrete graphical inference, independently labeled dataset preparation, frozen benchmark protocols, decimal cost accounting, and reproducible manuscript evidence. This release adds an explicitly bounded native OpenRouter execution contract for TypeSafe Jev, a separately defined Perplexity Decisions contract, and prospective interleaved native-model comparison protocols. The selected native hosted evidence contains 12 successful capability calls, including complete 77-way BANKING77 and 151-way CLINC option vocabularies, with reported billing of USD 0.000556920. These capability checks establish endpoint and task support; they do not establish dataset accuracy or calibrated probability meaning. Larger native hosted studies are ongoing and remain outside this release's completed research claims. Historical unknown billing and partial local results remain explicitly identified. Two native Mac Python profiles passed all 2,436 unit cases with combined coverage above 92%; package and manuscript reproduction were independently reviewed. The seven release assets contain the source, wheel, sdist, 30-page manuscript, selected evidence archive, release manifest, and checksums. Historical synthetic security-test canaries are retained as fixtures; real credentials, private journals, model weights, and raw corpora are excluded. Source build, artifact, and main commit identities are recorded separately in the release manifest.
items.title: daf-jev: Modular Decision Models, Orchestration, and Reproducible Evaluation

It integrates the raw datasets, Jupyter Notebooks, and the computational environment required to reproduce the study's findings. Archive Structure & Contents: The archive follows the standard directory structure: 1. /code (Analysis Workflows) Contains the Jupyter Notebooks used for network simulation and analysis, organized into four sub-directories corresponding to the resilience phases: 1. Preparedness/ : Scripts for initial network topology analysis. 2. Absorption/ : Scripts simulating the network's response to shock events. 3. Recovery/ : Scripts modeling the recovery possibility. 4. Adaptation/ : Scripts for structural optimization. 2. /data (Input Datasets) Contains the structural data used in the analysis, organized as follows: 35 cases (Initial data before adaptation and optimized data after adaptation)/ : Contains the adjacency matrices/edge lists for the 35 empirical ISNs (both baseline and optimized). Datasets for RRM/ : Data prepared for the Ridge Regression Model (RRM) analysis. Platform: Python (Jupyterlab). Base Environment: Python 3.8.8, JupyterLab 4.2.4. Key Python Packages: networkx 2.8.8 scikit-learn 1.3.2 numpy 1.24.4 pandas 2.0.3 matplotlib 3.7.5 scipy 1.10.1 openpyxl 3.1.0 4. /metadata Contains the metadata.yml file providing project authorship. items.summary: This repository contains the replication data and R code accompanying the study “From Periodic VAT Listings to Real-Time Reporting: Digital Reporting Requirements, Business Information Architecture and the EU VAT Compliance Gap”. The replication package combines European Commission VAT compliance gap data with a manually verified longitudinal coding of mandatory Digital Reporting Requirements across 26 European Union Member States over 2013–2023. The analytical panel contains 284 country-year observations. The policy coding harmonises periodic VAT listings and control statements, SAF-T and invoice-data reporting systems, and continuous or near-real-time transaction controls within a common information-governance framework. Alternative coding scenarios are retained to document uncertainty associated with implementation dates, phased rollouts and differences in reporting architecture. The accompanying R scripts reproduce the analytical dataset construction, descriptive statistics, two-way fixed-effects models, country-specific trend specifications, first-difference analysis, alternative treatment codings, architecture comparisons, panel diagnostics, staggered-adoption diagnostics and wild-cluster bootstrap inference reported in the study. No pre-computed analytical results are included in the repository. All derived results can be reproduced from the supplied input workbook and R scripts. The underlying VAT compliance gap data originate from the European Commission, Directorate-General for Taxation and Customs Union. The original DRR coding and its documentation were compiled by the authors from official European Commission and national tax-administration sources. The authors’ original data compilation and policy coding are made available under CC BY 4.0. The R replication code is released under the MIT License. Underlying third-party data remain subject to the terms of their original providers.
items.title: Replication Data and R Code for "From Periodic VAT Listings to Real-Time Reporting: Digital Reporting Requirements and the EU VAT Compliance Gap"

items.summary: This reproducibility compendium accompanies the study “From Prediction Accuracy to Process Robustness: Condition-Aware Stability Frontiers for Ti-6Al-4V Laser Powder Bed Fusion.” The study performs a condition-aware secondary analysis of open Ti-6Al-4V laser powder bed fusion melt-pool data to evaluate productivity-stability trade-offs beyond conventional prediction accuracy. The analysis quantifies scan-velocity-dependent changes in melt-pool width and variability, identifies Pareto-optimal operating conditions, derives epsilon-constrained process windows, models orientation anisotropy using a twofold circular harmonic formulation, and recomputes published row-random classifier metrics from the reported confusion matrix. The archive contains the condition-level source statistics used in the analysis, derived CSV outputs, Python analysis and figure-generation scripts, publication-ready figures, environment specifications, automated verification scripts, provenance metadata, a data dictionary, manuscript-to-result mappings, licensing information, and SHA-256 checksums. The package does not reconstruct synthetic individual-level observations from the underlying high-resolution dataset. All inferential results are based on reported process-condition summaries, consistent with the manuscript's condition-aware analytical framework.
items.title: "From Prediction Accuracy to Process Robustness: Condition-Aware Stability Frontiers for Ti-6Al-4V Laser Powder Bed Fusion."

items.summary: This document is the user guide and knowledge document for mosaeQ, a New Approach Methodology that computes preclinical safety predictions for a small molecule from quantum first principles, taking a SMILES string as its only input and using no training data. in Silico Pre-Clinical Regulatory Rehearsal Platform: mosaeQ.com It describes the Non-Euclidean Molecular Partitioning algorithm and the three-axis reference frame into which a molecule is embedded, the descriptors and rule-based assessments computed from that embedding, the four output formats the platform emits for each run, the provenance hashing applied to each run, and the endpoints explicitly excluded from the present release. It sets out an evaluation protocol for an independent laboratory, including hand recomputation of the reference-frame coordinates from the published ranges and a pre-registered benchmark executed under the evaluator's control on a reference set the supplier has not seen. Two annexes hold three worked examples in full —  aspirin, caffeine and chloroquine— giving the input file as imported and, for each compound, all four outputs the platform produces. The four outputs are generated by separate code paths, so they can be compared field by field. The outputs are labelled regulatory rehearsals. They are structured to the layouts that ICH, EMA and FDA expect and are aligned with those expectations. They are not a regulatory assessment and are not a substitute for any study those frameworks require. No value in the document is a dose recommendation. The platform is a beta release. Version strings are printed in every output and results can be compared only with results produced under the same versions. Files in this record are restricted; access may be requested from the record page.
items.title: mosaeQ Regulatory Rehearsal — User Guide and Knowledge Document, v1.3-beta

items.summary: This repository contains the supplementary computational material supporting the computer-assisted components of the article “The Three Gates: A Rooted-Operator Approach to Weil Positivity”. It includes source code, verification scripts, rigorous numerical certificates, machine-readable data, reference outputs, and reproducibility material for the finite computations used in the manuscript.   Version 4 consolidates the audited Gate-II verification package in parallel with the revised manuscript. items.summary: Welcome to WARP WARP (WDL Analysis Research Pipelines) repository is a collection of cloud-optimized pipelines for processing biological data from the Broad Institute Data Sciences Platform and collaborators. The contents of this repository are open source and released under the BSD 3-Clause license . Table of Contents WARP Overview Navigating WARP Using WARP WARP Versioning and Releasing Testing in WARP Feedback Acknowledgements WARP Overview WARP pipelines provide robust, standardized data analysis for the Broad Institute Genomics Platform and large consortia like the Human Cell Atlas and the BRAIN Initiative. You can count on WARP for rigorously scientifically validated, high scale, reproducible and open source pipelines. Our pipelines are written as "workflows" using the Workflow Description Language (WDL) and they process a broad spectrum of "omic" and array-related datasets (see the overview table below). | Pipeline Category | Data Types | | --- | --- | | Germline Variant Discovery | Genomes, Exomes | | Genotyping Arrays | Variant discovery, Chip validation, Joint array analysis | | Single-cell/nuclei Transcriptomics | Droplet based (10x Genomics), Smartseq2 | | Single-cell Epigenomics | Single nuclei ATAC-seq, Single nuclei MethylC-seq | | Joint Genotyping | Genomes, Exomes | | Somatic Alignment (beta) | Exomes | Try our pipelines in Terra , a platform for collaborative cloud analysis! Learn how in the Using WARP section. Navigating WARP All versioned and released pipelines are in one of the three pipelines subdirectories: broad (pipelines for the Broad Institute's Genomics Platform), cemba (pipelines for the BRAIN Initiative) or skylab (pipelines for the Human Cell Atlas Project). Each pipeline directory hosts a main workflow WDL that includes a pipeline version number and a corresponding changelog file. Workflows may call additional WDLs, referred to as tasks, that are located in the tasks directory. Pipelines that are in progress or have not yet been validated are in the beta-pipelines folder. Using WARP There are three ways to use WARP pipelines: 1. Download the workflow and run on a WDL-compatible execution engine WDL workflows run on multiple systems, including Cromwell , miniWDL , and dxWDL (see the openwdl documentation ). To run a pipeline's latest release, first navigate to WARP Releases , search for your pipeline's tag, and download the pipeline's assets (the WDL workflow, the JSON, and the ZIP with accompanying dependencies; see Optimus example below). You can also access a pipeline's release page by selecting the pipeline version number at the top of the pipeline's README. After downloading the pipeline's assets, launch the workflow following your execution engine's instructions. 2. Run the pipeline in Terra Several WARP pipelines are available in public workspaces on the Terra cloud platform. These workspaces include both the WDL workflow and downsampled data so that you can test the pipeline at low-cost. If you are new to Terra, you can get started by registering with your Google account and visiting Terra Support . After registration, search for WARP-related workspaces with the "warp-pipelines" tag. To test the pipeline, clone (make a copy of) the workspace following the instructions in this Terra Support guide . 3. Run or export the pipeline from Dockstore Dockstore is a GA4GH compliant open platform for sharing Docker-based tools like WDL workflows. You can find WARP pipelines in Dockstore and run them on the Dockstore platform or export them to other platforms (including Terra). To view all available pipelines, just search "warp" in the Dockstore search and browse the workflow list. See Dockstore documentation for details on launching the workflow. WARP Versioning and Releasing Pipelines in WARP are versioned semantically to support reproducibility in scientific analysis and provide clearer analysis provenance. Version numbers allow researchers to confirm their data has all been processed in a compati

items.summary: Welcome to WARP WARP (WDL Analysis Research Pipelines) repository is a collection of cloud-optimized pipelines for processing biological data from the Broad Institute Data Sciences Platform and collaborators. The contents of this repository are open source and released under the BSD 3-Clause license . Table of Contents WARP Overview Navigating WARP Using WARP WARP Versioning and Releasing Testing in WARP Feedback Acknowledgements WARP Overview WARP pipelines provide robust, standardized data analysis for the Broad Institute Genomics Platform and large consortia like the Human Cell Atlas and the BRAIN Initiative. You can count on WARP for rigorously scientifically validated, high scale, reproducible and open source pipelines. Our pipelines are written as "workflows" using the Workflow Description Language (WDL) and they process a broad spectrum of "omic" and array-related datasets (see the overview table below). | Pipeline Category | Data Types | | --- | --- | | Germline Variant Discovery | Genomes, Exomes | | Genotyping Arrays | Variant discovery, Chip validation, Joint array analysis | | Single-cell/nuclei Transcriptomics | Droplet based (10x Genomics), Smartseq2 | | Single-cell Epigenomics | Single nuclei ATAC-seq, Single nuclei MethylC-seq | | Joint Genotyping | Genomes, Exomes | | Somatic Alignment (beta) | Exomes | Try our pipelines in Terra , a platform for collaborative cloud analysis! Learn how in the Using WARP section. Navigating WARP All versioned and released pipelines are in one of the three pipelines subdirectories: broad (pipelines for the Broad Institute's Genomics Platform), cemba (pipelines for the BRAIN Initiative) or skylab (pipelines for the Human Cell Atlas Project). Each pipeline directory hosts a main workflow WDL that includes a pipeline version number and a corresponding changelog file. Workflows may call additional WDLs, referred to as tasks, that are located in the tasks directory. Pipelines that are in progress or have not yet been validated are in the beta-pipelines folder. Using WARP There are three ways to use WARP pipelines: 1. Download the workflow and run on a WDL-compatible execution engine WDL workflows run on multiple systems, including Cromwell , miniWDL , and dxWDL (see the openwdl documentation ). To run a pipeline's latest release, first navigate to WARP Releases , search for your pipeline's tag, and download the pipeline's assets (the WDL workflow, the JSON, and the ZIP with accompanying dependencies; see Optimus example below). You can also access a pipeline's release page by selecting the pipeline version number at the top of the pipeline's README. After downloading the pipeline's assets, launch the workflow following your execution engine's instructions. 2. Run the pipeline in Terra Several WARP pipelines are available in public workspaces on the Terra cloud platform. These workspaces include both the WDL workflow and downsampled data so that you can test the pipeline at low-cost. If you are new to Terra, you can get started by registering with your Google account and visiting Terra Support . After registration, search for WARP-related workspaces with the "warp-pipelines" tag. To test the pipeline, clone (make a copy of) the workspace following the instructions in this Terra Support guide . 3. Run or export the pipeline from Dockstore Dockstore is a GA4GH compliant open platform for sharing Docker-based tools like WDL workflows. You can find WARP pipelines in Dockstore and run them on the Dockstore platform or export them to other platforms (including Terra). To view all available pipelines, just search "warp" in the Dockstore search and browse the workflow list. See Dockstore documentation for details on launching the workflow. items.summary: Four command-line tools and one Claude Code plugin for keeping a paper's claims tied to what backs them. prereg freezes an analysis plan against a commit and a content hash before a run. results seals a run's inputs, records its outputs, and binds each number in a manuscript to the run behind it. citations checks that quoted passages appear in the sources they cite. repro verifies declared evidence assertions against pinned artifacts, reporting execution, extraction and comparison separately so that a value which disagrees, a value that is absent, and a check that never ran are three different answers.
items.title: reproducible-science: preregistration, citation verification, and results provenance

items.summary: Revolutionizing Environmental Data Stewardship: The U.S. National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI) is revolutionizing the stewardship of one of the world's most extensive environmental archives. This modernization effort is centered on the development and deployment of the Open Information Stewardship Service (OISS). OISS represents a paradigm shift from traditional data management to a cutting-edge, cloud-native knowledge mesh. The new cloud archive, OISS, is a key component within the broader National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service (NESDIS) Common Cloud Framework (NCCF), demonstrating NCEI's commitment to leveraging shared infrastructure. OISS is architected upon the highly scalable and reliable cloud technology, utilizing foundational services available within the NCCF. Technology Driving Open Science: At its technological core, OISS leverages the power of knowledge graphs within a semantically-enabled, linked open data interoperability framework. This potent combination delivers a platform that is inherently scalable, ensuring it can grow with the archive; repeatable, guaranteeing consistent service delivery; and entirely transparent, providing full and verifiable provenance for every element of environmental information it stewards. This framework is explicitly designed to ensure complete data lifecycle provenance, offering granular details on the origin, processing, and transformation of every dataset. Furthermore, it guarantees transparency in all stewardship operations and is fundamental to achieving scientific reproducibility. This architecture is aligned with critical U.S. federal mandates that champion open data and open science principles, ensuring NCEI's archive is accessible and trustworthy. Conclusions: The OISS is fundamentally transforming NCEI’s environmental archive services. This shift replaces traditional data management with a modern, cloud-native knowledge mesh. Built on cloud services within the NOAA NCCF, OISS leverages knowledge graphs and linked open data to create a scalable and transparent architecture. This framework ensures full data lifecycle provenance and scientific reproducibility, thereby aligning NCEI with U.S. federal open data mandates.
items.title: Transformation of NCEI's Environmental Data Stewardship
